description: Fix the 'Enable Notifications' infinite hang. Root cause: vite-plugin-pwa@2 with strategies:'injectManifest' does not register the SW in dev mode without devOptions.enabled:true, so navigator.serviceWorker.ready never resolves. Fix has three parts: (1) add devOptions to VitePWA in vite.config.js, (2) add a race-with-timeout guard in usePushNotifications.js so no await on navigator.serviceWorker.ready or pushManager.subscribe can hang forever, (3) surface the new 'sw-timeout' reason in NotificationPermission.jsx with a specific message, and fix the card's mobile position so it does not overlap the AIChat FAB.
steps: Step 1 — Read vite.config.js at C:\Users\abdul\Desktop\AIHABITTRACKER\frontend\ai-habit-tracker\vite.config.js. Inside the VitePWA({}) call, add 'devOptions: { enabled: true, type: "module" }' as a top-level key. Place it after the injectManifest block and before the manifest block. The existing keys (strategies, srcDir, filename, registerType, injectRegister, injectManifest, manifest) must remain unchanged.

Step 2 — Read src/hooks/usePushNotifications.js at C:\Users\abdul\Desktop\AIHABITTRACKER\frontend\ai-habit-tracker\src\hooks\usePushNotifications.js. Add a pure helper function above the export default: 'function withTimeout(promise, ms) { const timer = new Promise((_, reject) => setTimeout(() => reject(new Error("timeout")), ms)); return Promise.race([promise, timer]); }'. Then make these targeted replacements inside the hook: (a) In subscribe(): replace 'const reg = await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;' with 'let reg; try { reg = await withTimeout(navigator.serviceWorker.ready, 10_000); } catch { return { ok: false, reason: "sw-timeout" }; }'. (b) In subscribe(): wrap the pushManager.subscribe call in a try/catch: 'try { sub = await withTimeout(reg.pushManager.subscribe({...}), 10_000); } catch(err) { if (err?.message === "timeout") return { ok: false, reason: "sw-timeout" }; return { ok: false, reason: "network", error: err }; }'. (c) In unsubscribe(): replace the bare 'await navigator.serviceWorker.ready' with 'await withTimeout(navigator.serviceWorker.ready, 10_000)' (the existing outer try/catch already handles it). (d) In the useEffect that checks existing subscriptions: replace 'const reg = await navigator.serviceWorker.ready;' with 'const reg = await withTimeout(navigator.serviceWorker.ready, 10_000);' — the existing try/catch in that IIFE already handles the rejection.

Step 3 — Read src/components/NotificationPermission.jsx at C:\Users\abdul\Desktop\AIHABITTRACKER\frontend\ai-habit-tracker\src\components\NotificationPermission.jsx. Make two changes: (a) In handleEnable, add a new branch 'else if (res.reason === "sw-timeout") setStatus("sw-timeout");' before the final 'else setStatus("error");'. (b) In the JSX, add a new status message block: '{status === "sw-timeout" && (

Could not reach the notification service. Please refresh and try again.

)}' — place it alongside the other status blocks (denied, unsupported, unavailable, error). (c) Change the card's outer div position classes from 'fixed bottom-4 right-4' to 'fixed bottom-24 right-4 md:bottom-6 md:right-6' to prevent overlap with the AIChat FAB (which sits at bottom-20 md:bottom-6 right-6).
acceptance_criteria: vite.config.js VitePWA call contains devOptions: { enabled: true, type: 'module' }
usePushNotifications.js contains a withTimeout helper function
subscribe() in usePushNotifications.js returns { ok: false, reason: 'sw-timeout' } when navigator.serviceWorker.ready or pushManager.subscribe times out after 10 seconds
NotificationPermission.jsx handles status 'sw-timeout' and shows 'Could not reach the notification service. Please refresh and try again.'
NotificationPermission card is positioned at bottom-24 right-4 on mobile and md:bottom-6 md:right-6 on tablet+
npm run build completes with exit code 0 and emits dist/sw.js
findings: All three changes applied cleanly. Build exits 0; dist/sw.js and dist/manifest.webmanifest both present. One pre-existing warning: chunk > 500 kB (not related to this change). inlineDynamicImports deprecation warning from workbox is pre-existing and harmless.
